items.excerpt: Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start Saturday, including Jordan declaring three days of mourning after a deadly church attack that killed at least seven people, a US-brokered temporary ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, and a Russia-Ukraine prisoner swap of 270 servicemen. ## TOP STORIES ... Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said military officials are working to coordinate the ceasefire and that "those who wish to leave the town will be able to do so," adding that the operation requires extensive and complex preparations and that the evacuation is expected to take at least several days. - Russia, Ukraine swap 270 servicemen each in latest prisoner exchange Russian said Moscow and Kyiv swapped 270 servicemen each in the latest prisoner exchange between the two countries, with the returned Russian servicemen currently in neighboring Belarus. The Defense Ministry added that the service members will return to Russia after receiving necessary psychological and medical assistance and will be transported to medical facilities for further treatment and rehabilitation. ... - Israeli forces shot and killed two Palestinians in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron following allegations they opened fire at Israeli settlers, wounding five people. - Australia imposed sanctions on two North Korean companies and two financial brokers for their alleged role in funding Pyongyang’s nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs through fraudulent IT employment schemes. - Storm Austen left more than 160,000 households without power in France, as strong winds prompted weather alerts in 23 departments in the northwest. - A cybersecurity incident disrupted online systems in public schools in Richmond, capital of the US state of Virginia, forcing schools to shift to a technology-free learning environment while remaining open. - President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said Türkiye continues efforts to promote peace across regions, highlighting Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchanges and mediation initiatives in Africa. - The Collective Security Treaty Organization may decide on Armenia’s membership status at its summit in Moscow next month, with Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov saying the country’s withdrawal "could happen" if the issue is raised. - Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Ottawa is seeking Türkiye’s expertise to strengthen its defenses and build joint military capabilities, while rejecting US allegations of Canadian election interference and reaffirming that Canada will never become America’s 51st state. - International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol warned that the global energy crisis could persist into 2027, saying he sees little reason to expect a return to normal next year. - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the "immediate closure" of Hebron and instructed security forces to prepare a "full lockdown" of the occupied West Bank. - Greece’s parliament passed legislation banning children younger than 15 from accessing major social media platforms, with the measure set to take effect on Jan. 1. - Austria expelled four Russian diplomats for activities deemed incompatible with their diplomatic status, with the Foreign Ministry citing findings by security authorities but providing no details. - The Kremlin said the first tanker carrying Russian diesel fuel under a deal with the US has departed for its buyers, with additional shipments expected to continue regularly. - Russia said trilateral peace talks on Ukraine are scheduled for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, with discussions set to focus on security guarantees for Russia and Ukraine after a peace deal. - France will deploy 70,000 police officers and gendarmes ahead of nationwide protests, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez vowing an "extremely firm" response to violence, looting, and attacks on public buildings. - Ebola has spread to an eighth province in the Democratic Republic of Congo, as the UN food agency warns that hunger threatens treatment continuity for patients and 3.5 million people in outbreak-affected areas face crisis-level food insecurity. - The Pentagon released its seventh batch of UFO records, including reports of a fast-moving black triangular object spotted by federal agents near a secure US facility, historical sightings, and documents on alleged paranormal activity. - Canadian high diver Molly Carlson became the first woman to dive from a free-floating iceberg, completing a nearly 15-meter (49-foot) backward dive into freezing North Atlantic waters off Newfoundland and Labrador. - A new Israeli poll showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc losing three seats to 48, trailing the opposition bloc’s projected 54 seats ahead of the Oct. 27 election, with neither side projected to secure a governing majority. - Gold prices fell toward a three-month low as a selloff in technology stocks prompted investors to cover losses elsewhere, while rising oil prices fueled inflation concerns and expectations of higher interest rates.

items.title: Live Updates: Obama, Harris to campaign for Democrats in 3 battleground states; Trump travels to Georgia
items.excerpt: Live Updates: Obama, Harris to campaign for Democrats in 3 battleground states; Trump travels to Georgia ... President Trump has held rallies throughout the week in Iowa, Kansas, Florida and more, but leaders of the Democratic Party are set to hold a midterm blitz of their own on Saturday ahead of Election Day. Former President Obama is expected to make two Midwest trips to Cleveland, Ohio and Detroit, Mich. to help move the needle for Democrats in the two battleground states. Obama will first travel to Ohio to hold a rally with former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio), who is locked in a tight battle with Ohio Republican Jon Husted for the Buckeye State’s Senate seat. According to The Hill’s partner Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), Brown has a 51 percent chance to defeat Husted and is anticipated to be one of the tightest races in this year’s midterms. Following Obama’s Cleveland rally, he will travel north to Detroit to campaign with Michigan’s Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, who is facing former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.). DDHQ has El-Sayed holding a steady lead over Rogers, 68 percent to 32 percent, respectively. Former Vice President Harris will also be hitting the campaign trail on Saturday, meeting up with Democratic Senate candidate Chris Pappas (N.H.) in Portsmouth, N.H. Pappas is facing off against Republican challenger John Sununu for the chance to succeed Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.).

items.title: Trump makes Alaska the latest frontier in his election power grab - POLITICO
items.excerpt: President Donald Trump is escalating his crusade to exert control of America’s elections as his party barrels towards a potentially bruising midterm. The Justice Department has already filed lawsuits in nearly every state to try and gain access to voter files. Trump revisited his longstanding bid to restrict mail voting, sparking a legal battle that reached the Supreme Court. He sought to make anti-terrorism funds for state and local governments contingent on how they administer elections. He has threatened to withhold federal election funding from states that refuse to change voter registration forms and sparred with Republican lawmakers over a bill to overhaul elections. But with most of those efforts stalling, on Thursday, just 12 days before Election Day, the DOJ took things even further: In an extraordinary move, it asked a court to preemptively block Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. items.title: Box Office: 'Clayface' Takes No. 1, 'You Can See Everything' Follows
items.excerpt: # Box Office: ‘Clayface’ Lands at No. 1 with $10.4 Million Debut, ‘You Can See Everything’ Adds $6.14 Million on Friday ... Clayface might have been a considerably nicher choice for a feature film than DC’s “Supergirl” and “Superman,” but that didn’t stop audiences from showing out to catch the Batman supervillain’s gory, nightmare-inducing origin story at the box office this weekend. ... The new release generated $10.4 million from 3,458 North American theaters on Friday, taking the No. 1 spot. It’s a strong start for the film, which looks to pull in $24 million by Sunday. ... Directed by James Watkins, “Clayface” follows the titular Batman villain, a rising movie star also known as Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), who volunteers for a highly experimental medical procedure after his face is severely disfigured. Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan also star. Variety’s Guy Lodge called the film “its own ugly animal; perhaps the characters and conflicts introduced here would pall if given the franchise treatment, but in the context of a single, genre-melding romp, they’re fresh and ickily enjoyable.” ... A24’s much-hyped Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything” landed in second place on Friday, making $6.14 million from 2,655 North American theaters, up from 855 at opening weekend. The buzzy doc has made $31.7 million domestically so far. Rival estimates suggest the film will gross another $20 million by Sunday. Comedian Nathan Fielder and “Primetime” filmmaker Lance Oppenheim quietly worked on the movie for more than three years, which offers an unhinged look at the Theranos founder a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. In addition to being eligible for best documentary feature at the 99th Academy Awards, the film will also be submitted across the board as seen on A24’s awards site: best picture, director, production design, cinematography, costume design, film editing, makeup and hairstyling, sound and original score. Laika’s “ Wildwood,” another new release, landed in third place on Friday, grossing $4.28 million from 2,942 North American theaters. Featuring a voice cast that includes Carey Mulligan, Jacob Tremblay and others, the stop-motion film looks to bring in $11.2 million by Sunday. Directed by Travis Knight, “Wildwood” revolves around a teenage girl who travels with a classmate into an enchanted forest after her brother is abducted. Strong reviews should continue to propel the lavish film at the box office, which carries a substantial $100 million price tag. Black Bear’s “ Wicker” followed in fourth place, earning $2.36 million on Friday from 1,471 North American theaters. The offbeat romantic comedy, directed by Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer, is targeting a $5.5 million opening weekend. Described as an “audacious comedic fable,” “Wicker” tells the love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband from the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). Alexander Skarsgård plays said husband. Elizabeth Debicki also stars. ... Coming in fifth was Legendary Entertainment’s “Street Fighter.” The action film grossed $2.34 million on Friday and should add another $8.4 million by Sunday, bringing its cumulative gross to $46.7 million. ... “Street Fighter,” directed by Kitao Sakurai, stars Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji as two estranged fighters in the 90s who are recruited to enter a tournament that forces them to face off against each other.
